text:
elena: quick heads-up — started a small v2 shadow for tenant `atlas` at 09:03 PT to validate routing and quotas. noticed console shows quota burn on v1 for ~45s even though router traces indicate v2 handling. can someone eyeball telemetry?

ux-bot: note: shadow-mode enabled for tenant=atlas @2025-06-11T16:03:02Z. dashboards default to billing_meter aggregation.

anya: i'm seeing the same. router logs: chosen_route=v2 (shadow=true) for sampled reqs, but quota logs record meter_key=v1 for a subset. this feels like binding between tenant and meter_key is still using last-known binding until a reconciliation job runs.

rob: we have a background reconciliation cron that maps tenant -> billing_key every 2m to amortize DB reads. shadow flips don't update the binding immediately — by design. might be surprising in the UI.

mike: oh — that reconciliation delay could be interpreted as v2 failing. PMs will assume the canary is hurting rates. we should make the temporary discrepancy explicit.

elena: two quick asks: 1) can we show a “binding_state” indicator on the tenant routes page (values: active|pending-reconcile|stale) so console users see when billing mapping is catching up? 2) can we suppress quota-alerts triggered by shadow-mode until binding_state == active?

rob: infra side: adding a lightweight pubsub emit when shadow-mode toggles is low-risk. billing can mark binding as pending and then run an immediate rebind rather than waiting for cron. i'll prototype a rebind-on-change path.

anya: telemetry: we can compute a per-tenant mismatch ratio (percent of sampled traces where chosen_route != meter_key) and surface it as `attribution_mismatch_pct`. that will help ops triage.

opsbot: runtime-change: add sampling override for tenant=atlas => trace.sample=100% for 30m per elena request.

elena: thanks opsbot. running a few tests now. also, UX suggestion: while the reconcile is pending, show a small inline banner next to the route toggle: "Quota attribution pending sync — expected within ~2m" with a link to docs. small copy change.

mike: follow-up: we should also add a “rollout safety” check that requires billing binding to be active before escalating canary percent above 10%. otherwise teams will misinterpret metrics. add to canary runbook.

rob: agree. implementing immediate invalidation + eager rebind on tenant-routing:update. plan: publish a `tenant-binding:pending` event, billing will call rebind endpoint and then emit `tenant-binding:active` when done. will add trace/span around rebind so we can measure latency.

anya: analytics will add `attribution_mismatch_pct` and a dashboard tile. also will add an alert that flags mismatch_pct > 20% for >1m during a route-change. but that alert will be suppressed for tenants with shadow-mode=true to avoid noise.

elena: i ran the shadow for 90s. mismatch peaked at 32% for the first 30s then dropped under 2% after the eager rebind. good proof-of-concept.

ux-bot: suggestion: add a console toggle (checkbox) "wait-for-billing-bind before increasing canary" in the rollouts UI. default off but recommended.

mike: i like that. small UX change plus a guard in the backend to reject percent increases >10% if binding_state != active and runbook flag not set.

rob: i'll add the publish/rebind bits and a small e2e that verifies binding_state transitions and that percent-change is blocked when binding_state!=active. targeting staging deploy today.

anya: analytics will expose last_binding_sync_ts and compute sync_age. will use that to auto-suppress quota-based alerts for recent flips (<3m).

elena: owners: rob infra (rebind-on-update + guard), anya analytics (mismatch metric + suppression), mike UX (binding_state indicator + rollouts toggle + toast copy). i'll file a short RFC and link the staging PRs.

mike: one more note: update docs for on-call runbook — include steps: check binding_state, sample traces, don't rollback solely on billing spikes until sync_age>3m.

opsbot: reminder created: RFC-6078 "eager billing binding + rollout guard" assigned to rob, due next Wed.

elena: thanks all, closing once RFC and PRs linked. :thumbsup:
